data.source_title: Prospective comparison of magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography in diagnosing occult scaphoid fractures
data.locator: PubMed abstract; patients with negative radiographs and negative CT underwent MRI.
data.source_setting: Prospective diagnostic cohort; suspected scaphoid fracture after wrist trauma; CT after two negative radiographs at 7-10 days, followed by MRI for eligible CT-negative patients.
data.source_period: Published 2023; recruitment dates not stated in abstract.
data.source_n: 100 included patients with negative radiographs and CT.
data.quantity: MRI findings after negative radiographs and CT

scaphoid_fracture.denominator_status: Abstract says of these fractures; intended denominator is ambiguous.

fracture_or_bruise_referred_hand_surgery.reported_rate: 25% of patients with fractures and bone bruising; numerator and denominator not given

data.source_evidence_basis: Abstract reports MRI fractures in 16% of 100 patients (15 patients), scaphoid fracture 8%, bone bruising 10%, and hand-surgery referral for 25% of patients with fracture/bone bruising. The 15/100 count calculates to 15%, inconsistent with the abstract’s 16%; both source wording and count are preserved without resolving the discrepancy.
data.limitations: Selected CT-negative second-line cohort. Abstract percentage/count conflict for any fracture (16% versus 15/100); hand-surgery referral numerator and denominator are not specified. Keep those quantities uncalibrated pending full paper. Scaphoid percentage wording does not establish an 8/100 count. Do not infer subgroup numerators from rounded percentages.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Calibration only for a second-line CT-negative pathway; keep separate from initial negative-radiograph scenarios and do not infer universal hand-surgery referral.
